reason: The ablation requirement can reject a correctly identified intersection key. Let U={a,b,c}, constraint1={a,b}, constraint2={a,c}. Their intersection uniquely selects a, but removing either nonredundant constraint leaves two possibilities. design.mechanism: intersection-selected key versus arbitrary best single-channel gloss
design.unit: held complete constructions or paired reading contexts
design.contrast: A held form should retain the same commitment when any one training channel is removed; a single-channel gloss should change or become underdetermined.
design.prediction: GDT360 and GDT832 combine channels for prediction but do not require a finite semantic commitment to survive leave-one-channel-out permutation.
design.countermodel: A surface-copying, renderer, or context-conditioned convention can mimic training observations without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: The commitment changes under removal of one nonredundant channel, or all permutations tie after honest capacity control.
design.principal_risk: Independent channels may be dependent and no readable plaintext anchor is currently available.
design.smallest_test: Freeze three constraint families, learn on two, then leave one family out on a held form and inspect whether the candidate commitment remains uniquely ranked.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Near GDT360/GDT832; distinct falsifier is commitment stability under channel ablation, not score improvement.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim

all_of.detail: Provide a finite source-specific contract that addresses this recorded design objection and a rival with different observable predictions. Independently bound words are not a blanket prerequisite for exploratory joint inference.

not_sufficient: A new model, renderer, larger corpus or more matching formal labels without resolving the recorded objection.

claim_ceiling: Original proposal preserved; no empirical semantic refutation or confirmed meaning.
